brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.requirement: Planter suitable for sunny kitchen windowsill (compact linear form, ~3 cells wide)
requirements.evidence: 3-cell linear arrangement (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,-1,0;full) with 3x hex-bin-full bins; compact ~265mm wide, fits windowsill footprint; caps and joint bolts provide finished enclosure

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full planted basil-young (prop:1), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full planted mint-young (prop:2), bin:0,-1,0~hex-bin-full planted parsley-young (prop:3); all bins filled with soil via fill_and_plant

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell windowsill planter with three full-depth bins, each filled with soil and planted with a different herb (basil, mint, parsley). House rules applied (capped open faces, locked joints) and verified mesh-clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
